comparison: Perfect agreement on dataset quality (C1, C24, C25, C77, C80, C81). Both evaluations find the dataset impressive and comprehensive with no concerns raised about sample sizes or data provenance.
Complete agreement on sex-specific seasonal effects (C4, C52). Both evaluations support the finding that females show microbiome age effects during dry season while males do not.

Full agreement on rank effects (C5, C54, C56, C70, C71). Both evaluations affirm the sex-specific rank-associated variation in microbiome aging pace, despite OpenEval noting the effect is 'relatively weak and noisy' for males.

Agreement on methodological explanations (C100, C101, C102). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature, while peer reviewers highlight the methods as a major strength without challenging the explanations.

Strong agreement on microbiome clock development (C2, C42, C43, C62, C63). Both find the clock's predictive accuracy compelling, though peer result also includes C67 (comparison to human clocks) which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Agreement on age-associated compositional changes (C34-C40). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing, though peer result also includes C41 and C98 (taxonomic comparisons) which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

Agreement on null mortality findings (C6, C7, C61). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to methodological limitations (censored data, small samples), while peer reviewers accept the negative finding with acknowledgment of gaps to be addressed in future work. Peer result also includes C105.

Agreement on sex-stratified model performance (C44, C45, C46). Both evaluations support these findings. Peer result also includes C3 and C64 (sex differences in aging rates) which OpenEval addresses separately in R6.
Agreement on sex differences in microbiome aging rates (C3, C64). Both evaluations affirm this finding as clear and exciting evidence, with OpenEval providing detailed statistical support.
Agreement on data quality and processing (C83, C84). Both evaluations support the technical quality, with peer result also including C85 and noting the analysis is extensive and high-level.

Partial agreement on limitations (C68). Both acknowledge microbiome clock performs worse than epigenetic clocks. Peer result also includes C69 (population specificity) which OpenEval addresses separately in R18.
Agreement on population specificity limitation (C69). Both evaluations acknowledge the microbiome clock's limited generalizability across populations as an important constraint.
Agreement on individual-level consistency (C50). Both evaluations support the variance partitioning findings showing substantial individual consistency in microbiome age deviations.
Agreement on null cumulative adversity finding (C60). Both evaluations accept this negative result, with OpenEval explaining it by conflicting effects of different adversity sources.

Agreement on temporal dynamics interpretation (C8, C65). Both evaluations support the conclusion that microbiome age reflects current conditions rather than early-life adversity. Peer result also includes C66 which OpenEval addresses in R15.
Partial overlap on temporal dynamics (C105). OpenEval groups this with C8 and C65 to support recency model interpretation, while peer reviewers accept it as part of the null mortality findings.

Agreement on background context (C26-C33). Both evaluations support the characterization of the study population and environment, with peer reviewers highlighting the ability to characterize social and physical environments as a major strength.

Agreement on taxonomic comparisons (C41, C98). Both evaluations support the species-specific patterns of microbiome aging. OpenEval also includes C95, C96, C97 which are not explicitly mentioned in peer result.

Partial agreement on integration with other biomarkers (C66). OpenEval groups this with C72-C74 to show convergence across aging biomarkers, while peer result focuses on environmental and social variables impacting microbiome aging.
Agreement on comparison to human clocks (C67). OpenEval addresses this separately with C22-C23, while peer reviewers include it with overall clock development findings (C2, C42, C43, C62, C63).
OpenEval identifies potential data leakage limitation (C87) that could inflate model performance. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this methodological concern.

OpenEval synthesizes findings on convergence of multiple aging biomarkers (C66, C72, C73, C74) showing high rank in males associates with accelerated aging. No direct corresponding peer evaluation, though peer reviewers generally affirmed rank-related findings.
